generic_sampling_rules.text_categorical: sample from a small pool of 3-12 distinct strings; for a column with a LIKE/equality target create exact literal plus near-variants (case change, trailing 'x', trailing ' x', prefix/suffix '%' forms) with near-variant share 15-30%
generic_sampling_rules.text_name_like: sample from a name pool; on DISTINCT-target columns repeat values so duplicate share is 20-50%
generic_sampling_rules.integer_id: sequential distinct integers starting at 1; never NULL; on join columns reserve specific parent ids as childless (~20-30% of parents) and only rarely ~5-10% NULL child foreign keys when the child column is nullable
generic_sampling_rules.integer_quantity_positive: uniform integer in [1, max_observed]; never 0; one NULL row per instance on nullable integer columns
generic_sampling_rules.real_amount: uniform real in [0.1, 1.5 * max_observed], rounded to 1 decimal; non-negative; include boundary values at listed literals: literal-0.1, literal, literal+0.1, literal+1 when a comparison target is given
generic_sampling_rules.date: ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'; for date pairs keep first <= second
generic_sampling_rules.enum_short: pick from explicit value list given in per_column_exceptions
generic_sampling_rules.tie_and_order_columns: on an ORDER target column place at least two rows tied at each listed rank with the listed direction (e.g. 2 rows at maximum value for DESC rank 1); never overwrite a planted boundary literal or near-variant to create the tie
generic_sampling_rules.group_size_pattern: for GROUP-target columns arrange group cardinalities: at least one value appearing once, one appearing twice, and one appearing >=3 times; verify after all other mutations
generic_sampling_rules.null_rule: each instance has at least one NULL row for every nullable column; NULL share approx observed null rate (0% observed -> still plant >=1 NULL); NULL never replaced to satisfy a rule; rules constrain non-NULL values only; NOT NULL and primary-key columns never get NULL
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_value_share: when a pool is exhausted use fresh values with share 10-20%
generic_sampling_rules.pk_uniqueness: primary keys (single or composite) are generated sequentially/without collision against compact rows and within the block; composite keys are deduped as tuples

targets.integer_valued_real_ids: 1.0,2.0,... sequential distinct, no collision with compact rows

targets.joint_verification: all four targets hold simultaneously after all mutations

generation_specification.uncertainty: Column statistics say company has 19 rows but the sample shows 8 and employment 5; sample row 5 of employment has no Year_working (list shorter). Statistics assert 0% nulls everywhere yet nullable columns exist; we still plant >=1 NULL where allowed. employment.Company_ID is declared INT while company.Company_ID is REAL - FK type mismatch tolerated as integer-valued reals. Industry and Headquarters have 5 and 8 distinct observed values but the sample is partial; enum pools derived from statistics and sample. No calculated columns found in the sample, so no formulas beyond range/enum rules. employment.Company_ID is NOT NULL per schema and per_column_exceptions, so it is removed from null_targets; nullable columns (people.Age, people.Name, people.Nationality, people.Graduation_College, company.Name, company.Headquarters, company.Industry, company.Sales_in_Billion, company.Profits_in_Billion, company.Assets_in_Billion, company.Market_Value_in_Billion, employment.Year_working) each receive at least one NULL row per instance.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: n_ok=0, n_fail=20, errors={'RowsSkipped': 20}, rows_skipped={'people': 86, 'company': 84}. Every instance failed because the writer reports RowsSkipped>0 (cli._one sets ok=False when sum(skipped.values())>0). The generator is supposed to produce zero skipped rows by construction.
issues.requested_revision: Fix the row construction so that no INSERT is rejected. The dominant cause is PK collisions: spec_sampler._dedup_against_inst only dedups single-column PKs against schema.original_values, but company.Company_ID and people.People_ID are drawn by NumberSampler (random ints) and collide with compact rows and with each other; employment has a composite PK (Company_ID, People_ID) that is never deduped at all. Generate sequential distinct PKs (integer_id rule: 'sequential distinct integers starting at 1') for people.People_ID and company.Company_ID, and dedup the composite employment PK against compact rows and within the block. Re-run until n_fail=0 and rows_skipped is empty.

issues.evidence: spec_sampler._sample_fk leaves ~20-30% of parent ids childless by sampling a subset of parent keys, but the spec's unmatched_join_rows target is 'parent_rows_without_children: true' for both employment.Company_ID->company and employment.People_ID->people. With block sizes company=10, people=7, employment=8, sampling 70-80% of parents and drawing 8 children with replacement does not guarantee any parent is childless; and the same _sample_fk is used for both FKs independently, so the composite PK can also collide. Additionally, employment.Company_ID is forced allow_null=False (correct per spec 'null_share: none (NOT NULL)'), but the generic null_rule in build_spec_rows then plants NULLs in every other nullable column including employment.Year_working (feedback shows NULL 20/136) — acceptable per interface, but the FK childless guarantee is not enforced.
issues.requested_revision: Construct employment rows so that at least one company.Company_ID and at least one people.People_ID from the generated parent block have no child row (e.g. reserve specific parent keys as childless before sampling children), and ensure the composite (Company_ID, People_ID) pairs are unique. Keep employment.Company_ID non-NULL.

issues.evidence: spec_sampler._inject_hq and _force_groups: _force_groups overwrites values with items[0..2] from the current Counter, which can destroy the LIKE near-variants ('USA%','%USA%','usa','USB','USA x','USAx') and the tied rank-1 DESC maximum that _inject_hq just planted. _inject_hq then re-checks the max tie but not the near-variant share or the 1/2/3+ group sizes after _force_groups. The spec requires all of: group_sizes 1/2/3+, duplicate_share 20-50%, tie_at_rank [1] DESC, and near_variant_share 15-30% simultaneously on company.Headquarters.
issues.requested_revision: Make the Headquarters construction satisfy all four targets jointly and verify them after all mutations (assert group sizes {1,2,>=3}, near-variant share in [0.15,0.30], duplicate share in [0.20,0.50], and >=2 rows at the max value). Do not let _force_groups clobber planted near-variants or the max tie.

issues.evidence: spec_sampler._inject_sales places boundary literals then forces a max tie, but _num_group is applied to Profits/Assets and _coerce_numeric runs after _company_patterns; the spec requires Sales_in_Billion comparison_boundary values [199.9,200.0,200.1,200.9,201.0,201.1] AND ties_for_order_limit rank 1 DESC with '>= 2 rows with different values'. With n=10 and 6 boundary values plus a forced max tie, the boundary set may be truncated (placed>=n break) and the max tie may overwrite a boundary value. Also _num_group sets all values to a/b/c, which for Profits/Assets is fine but the group-size guarantee is not verified.
issues.requested_revision: Guarantee all six boundary values are present when n>=6 (block size is 10, so feasible), keep the max tie without overwriting a boundary literal, and assert the group-size pattern for Profits_in_Billion and Assets_in_Billion after construction.

issues.evidence: Specification 'uncertainty' notes: 'Column statistics say company has 19 rows but the sample shows 8 and employment 5; sample row 5 of employment has no Year_working'. The semantic rules (Age BETWEEN 18 AND 70, Year_working > 0, non-negative amounts, Industry enum) are supported by the sample but the row-count and null-rate evidence is contradictory. The spec also declares null_targets=['employment.Company_ID'] while the schema and per_column_exceptions say employment.Company_ID is NOT NULL ('null_share: none (NOT NULL)') — a direct contradiction.
issues.requested_revision: Resolve the contradiction: remove employment.Company_ID from null_targets (it is NOT NULL per schema and per_column_exceptions), and state the intended table sizes / null shares explicitly rather than relying on the contradictory statistics. The semantic range/enum rules are adequately evidenced and can stay.

issues.evidence: Construction feedback: construction_pairs eligible=38, separated=10. Many atomic-operation pairs are not separated by the generated instances. While a missing separation alone does not prove an error, the RowsSkipped failures mean the instances that would exercise these pairs were never fully written (n_ok=0), so separation cannot be assessed reliably.

Report the separated count per group.

issues.title: people.Age NULL planted while the spec's main formula expects non-NULL ages
issues.evidence: Spec semantic rule: people.Age BETWEEN 18 AND 70 (evidence: observed 25-37). The generic null_rule instructs a NULL in every nullable column, but the program's `_people_patterns` writes `rng.randint(18,70)` for all ages, and the generic `_apply_null_rule` (in build_spec_rows' final NULL loop) then overwrites one age with NULL. Execution feedback confirms 'people.Age: generated rows: NULL 20 / 148' — one NULL per instance. Three-valued logic makes 'NULL BETWEEN 18 AND 70' NOT FALSE, so this does not violate the rule, but it is worth flagging because the sample had no NULL ages and the age-range formula reads as an always-true invariant.
issues.revision_request: Optional: restrict the planted NULL on people.Age (e.g. treat the age-range rule as an always-true invariant and skip nulling, or document that NULL is allowed under three-valued logic). No change is required for correctness; the rule holds under the NULL-as-value interface.

issues.title: Spec uncertainty notes vs. executed construction; several targets unverified by execution
issues.evidence: The spec's 'uncertainty' block flags conflicting row counts (statistics say company 19 rows, sample shows 8), a missing Year_working in one sample row, 0% NULL statistics vs. nullable columns, and an FK type mismatch (employment.Company_ID INT vs company.Company_ID REAL). The program handles these (table_sizes_per_instance overrides the row count, `_coerce_numeric` and sequential PK starts cope with REAL ids, NULL rule is applied explicitly). Execution shows n_ok=20, n_fail=0, zero FK/not-null/PK violations, and 0 skipped rows. However, construction_pairs reports only 10 of 38 eligible pairs 'separated' (construction_pairs_by_group is empty, so the per-target breakdown — e.g. the four joint Headquarters targets, sales boundary/tie, group sizes — is not shown in the feedback).
issues.revision_request: Not blocking: the program ran cleanly and implements the specified domains and dependency order (people -> company -> employment; FK draws from in-memory parents; composite PK dedup). Request the engineer/designer surface construction_pairs_by_group so the Headquarters joint-target, Sales boundary/tie, and group-size targets can be confirmed; a missing pair separation alone does not prove a generation error.
